utterances.text: (Handed). Your Honours, this is again a tape that was handed to Officer Panzer by the accused Mucic during the course of the execution of the search warrant on his premises. At page 6503 and 6504, when shown this particular video, Officer Panzer said in relation to it: "This video is one I recognise on the basis of the label and the sticker which I put on there. That is my writing on there. On the first line, it says 'Celbit' that I recognise. There are two videos we found at Mr. Mucic's apartment that had such a reference. One of them said 'Celbit' and the other said 'Celebici' on it. I had a look at all four videotapes. MID, this tape, I believe, has the footage where Mr. Mucic can be seen together with other people in uniform. They are in a room and there is singing and drinking going on there." Your Honours, this videotape shows the relationship between the accused Mucic as commander of the camp and the guards that are under his command. It is a very long tape, but it does contain -- we have extracted very short segments of it, because of primarily the people that appear and the relationship that exists between them. There is a reference to a witness that has testified and testified that he was present at this party, and that is in the very first segment. Then there is, in the second segment, there is a reference to Hazim, there is music playing. Then at the very bottom of the segment 2, there is a question by the harmonica player: "Are they lacking anything?", and the accused Mucic says: "What they might be missing is some beating." Then there is a reference following that to Borci. Again a reference to the witness who testified, and then we see a voice says: "You will go with me and the commander. We will give you a gun but you must shoot at your own people. "Mucic: You never know where he will shoot. We will keep him under control. "Soldier: We will take care about him, commander." Then we go over to segment 4, it is a reference there to going to Borci, and your Honours are aware of other evidence that you have been referred to in relation to Borci, and the role that it played -- the significance of it during this particular time. There is towards the bottom a reference there, where it starts: "Zara, you will tie me and him and pretend that you captured us. Then you must tell them to let us go or you will shoot them", et cetera et cetera. Then a voice says: "He must take us to one of their nests", and so forth: "Mucic: And what then? "Voice: Then we will throw in a hand grenade." Your Honours, having regard to the fact that this video was handed to Officer Panzer by the accused Mucic in response to his questions as to what he wanted when he was executed the search warrant, having regard to its contents and its relationship to other matters upon which your Honours have had testimony or evidence, it is our submission that this is a video that should properly be admitted into evidence. Your Honours, you asked me to address you on the question of the videos that were recovered from the INDA-BAU premises and where there was a difficulty with the numbering. Your Honours, this in our submission was the subject of your Honours' decision in relation to it on 12th September 1997 at page 7406 of the transcript, where your Honour Judge Karibi-Whyte, when delivering the decision of the Chamber, said: "We are giving a very short ruling on the last of the arguments, because of the nature of the decision we are handing down. "The Trial Chamber has considered the contentions of counsel for Delalic and for the Prosecution, with respect to the admissibility of evidence consisting of documents and video cassettes recovered during the search of premises designated as occupied by Delalic in those proceedings." That is the INDA-BAU premises and there was a premises where no documents have been tendered in relation to: "We have considered the contention that the warrant relied upon for the search of the premises is illegal. The Trial Chamber has no evidence of the breach of any conditions predicating its issue. We rely on the principle of omnia presumatorite esse acta to hold the warrant valid. The effect of non-compliance with the procedure requirements of such, we do not consider the situation so reprehensible as to render the acts illegal. We therefore consider it in the interests of the trial to admit the material recovered during the search. We therefore consider it in the interests of the trial to admit the materials recovered during the search and tendered in evidence. "We however observe that the Defence is entitled to address the Trial Chamber on those materials, and will be entitled to challenge the admissibility of any documents sought to be tendered as arising from the search or discrepancies from evidence of witnesses. This is because the Prosecution is seeking to tender 12 folders containing documents but not the documents contained therein." Your Honour is quite right, we have never sought to tender the documents contained in those folders: "To adopt another approach would be tantamount to reviewing a considerable portion of the case, an exercise clearly undesirable in the overall determination of the case, which should not be decided piecemeal. The Defence is entitled to challenge any of the evidence when tendered. They still reserve the right to challenge any other issues which are not involved in this decision. "I think this is our decision. We will carry on in this way. We will deliver our ruling on the Mucic admissibility letter later on, not now. We can now go into a status conference." At that stage, Madam Residovic rises and says: "Your Honour, with your permission, to make sure that it is clear to me in this phase, this was your decision regarding the documents and 12 folders. However, in the proposal of the Prosecution -- in the motion of the Prosecution, there were three videotapes that Mr. Navrat, the only witness from the location, could neither identify nor recognise, nor did the Prosecutor propose that to the witness, and in your decision, I did not hear whether you decided -- whether you have already ruled on the three videotapes whose number changed from the time of the seizure to the time they departed from the police station, so I would like to ask you if I misunderstood, because I thought the ruling referred only to the documents. I would like to have a clarification at this point. Thank you very much." Then your Honour, Judge Karibi-Whyte then responds: "What I said was consisting of documents and video cassettes. That was what I said. Perhaps the transcript will show that." Clearly, your Honour's transcript does precisely that. In our submission, your Honours, the issue of the numbering as an irregularity has by that decision been ruled upon, and your Honours have ruled in favour of the submission of the Prosecution in that regard, but your Honours did preserve the right for the accused to argue other matters other than the question of legality of the search warrant and questions pertaining to the procedures adopted at the time, so in our submission, your Honours, your Honour's decision is quite clear and indeed was rendered even more clear by the fact that Madam Residovic rose immediately after your Honours had delivered your ruling on this question and specifically and precisely asked you that question in relation to the mis-numbering of the video, and your Honour quite rightly responded that your ruling covered not only the documents but the videos as well, and that that would be reflected in the transcript, which indeed it was. In our submission, your Honours, that question has been ruled upon by your Honours, but there are other matters obviously that the Defence may choose to argue, which your Honours have preserved for them to do so by that ruling. Your Honour, the first of those videos that were recovered from the premises, I22 --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, are you entertaining argument on the interpretation of your decision? You pointed out to Mr. Niemann you wanted to discuss with him the better of the discrepancies; now he has offered an interpretation of your decision and we have not heard from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually I am not sure he is going to discuss the fact that the observations which were reserved to a later date have been taken care of. You still have the opportunity to challenge the particular tapes, because not being sure which tapes were recovered from there, you still have the opportunity of doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, the first tape, Exhibit 114, was a tape of an interview that was given by General Pasalic in May 1992 in relation to events that occurred in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Before you continue, the attitude which we took then, and which we still do take now, is that there was a confusion in the number of tapes recovered. There is no doubt that tapes were recovered or were claimed to have been recovered at the INDA-BAU premises, but because of numbering irregularities one was not sure whether there were additional tapes from elsewhere or whether it was a mere miscalculation of how many tapes there were. The problem now is which of the tapes, which they are entitled to challenge, which of the tapes are additional to those which were found on the premises and those which were shown to have been counted at the police headquarters, because from one premises to the other there was an increase. You have to show exactly how to explain that discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I also refer to a situation or circumstance? Navrat appeared in the witness box and he insisted upon the number which he had mentioned in his report. Nobody asked him from the Prosecution side, "could you be mistaken about the number?" That discrepancy had already come to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will need to examine the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You see the question is, if there are three additional tapes, which ones are those? Is it the one now which you are offering? That is the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is not certain which are the additional tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution could have simply asked him, "could you have been mistaken in your counting?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will need to look at the transcript. I did not take the witness so I will need to examine the transcript to see what was said. What I do know is that the tapes that are before your Honours were specifically dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He dealt with 54. Only 51 were recovered, according to Navrat. He might have dealt with the tapes -- because Moerbauer was not there. There is a doubt, that is all I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is still lingering. That doubt has not been cleared, that there were additional tapes. Now when you do whichever tapes you do now, it is not easy for you to say with certainty, "These were the tapes recovered from the premises".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe the one which you are referring to now was not one of the original 51. Mr. Navrat could have been simply asked, "Could you have been mistaken?", and he could have said, "I was in a hurry, I had to go somewhere else, maybe I left it to someone else to count them, I took the figure as it was". He could have given so many explanations, but you did not ask him for explanations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I did not take the witness, your Honour. Your Honour, the point that I make though is that the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is a criminal trial and we have to be very clear that the evidence we admit is really the evidence which was recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: All I am saying is that it is not a matter of speculation, there is evidence here which specifically deals with it. That is the only evidence that deals with these particular tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There is uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It does not appear to be uncertainty from the evidence, your Honours. The evidence seems to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Navrat's statement is clear. As it is under the criminal law which we administer the benefit of any reasonable doubt has to go to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As to his guilt or innocence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I agree with that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The trouble is the prosecution seems to be sure or certain about the tapes recovered. Every other person who is familiar with this case knows that there is uncertainty about the number of tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless I have misunderstood the words of your Honours' ruling, I thought the question of the chain of evidence had been resolved. Certainly it has been addressed in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, that was why it was left to the Defence to challenge any attempt to bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I made a submission on chain, an extensive submission on the chain of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Tapes were recovered, whether 51 or 53, but some tapes were recovered, and we left the Defence with the opportunity of challenging whenever they are being tendered in evidence. We have heard a discrepancy, which came to the notice of the Prosecution a long time ago when Moerbauer was appearing in the witness box. The Prosecution should have cleared that up when Navrat appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I made a lengthy submission on this issue, and I assumed your Honours had decided. From my reading of your Honours' decision, I thought you had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What did your submission lead to, that one figure was the accurate figure?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My submission related to the legality of the search, the procedures adopted by the officers at the time and the question of the chain of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That does not mean that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have no reason to doubt the integrity of the Austrian police officers. They spoke the truth. They did make a count. The question is: how many tapes did they count?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is the chain of evidence, I would have thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Moerbauer merely comes in 22 days later; when he examines these tapes, he finds 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is not chain of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Anyway, it could not be accepted that those tapes were all those tapes recovered from the premises. It would not be acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In relation to the tape that was shown to General Pasalic at least, which is already admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Pasalic said that he did make the statement. Fair enough, you can have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is in evidence. That was also affected by the mis-numbering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: But here is a person who made that statement on the television, which was taped; he said, "I did make the statement", so that in itself is sufficient, not because it was found in INDA-BAU. The fact that the person who appeared in that picture says, "I made this tape, this refers to me", is sufficient to prove that tape. You do not have to go to the testimony of the Austrian police officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You do not have to go anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will make submissions to your Honours on the question, then, of chain of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is not a question of chain of evidence, it is a question of tapes were recovered and Moerbauer examines them, he finds them to be 54. You could have easily cleared the position when Navrat appeared in the witness box. You could have said to him, "You only recovered 51 but from the box which you presented Moerbauer, there are 54", and he could have given an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can recall Moerbauer, if your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would that help, if he again said, "I saw 54"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I could put to him that he made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Who made the mistake, Navrat or Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will call both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Because Moerbauer has listed 54, so he knows that he has 54 tapes. Navrat has listed 51, he says, "I recovered 51", so how would recalling them help to clear this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour was just saying to me a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you want to call them, you should call Navrat, not Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can do that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And then he will come and say, "I had 54 instead of 51"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no idea what he will say, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You had the opportunity, you did not avail yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I did not speak to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The discrepancy had already come to the notice of the Prosecution and the Defence. You should have cleared it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What you want to do is to deal with the content of those tapes as recovered from INDA-BAU premises. This is where it comes into issue. I think we will have a break. It is 5.30. You can go and think of how to resolve it. I am afraid there is no way open to me now to allow those tapes as they are, for the content of those tapes. I am not sure about what they contain, but when you get to the contents, you can tell me whether they can be used at all, because you are not sure which of them is from the premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is a discrepancy also about the number of documents, but that is a matter which has not really come up. I think 28 or 31, something like that, I forget now. I am just speaking from memory, but there was a discrepancy about the number of documents also.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I addressed all of this in my chain of evidence submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, but it depends on the contents which have to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you can find an answer to this problem tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I envisage at this stage I will be recalling all these officers. I think I need to recall all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and meet again at 10.00 tomorrow morning.

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
